sentences.text: This i s first application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.679/2022 (Crime No.679/2023 as wrongly mentioned in his application) dated 13.09.2022 registered at Police Station Rampur Naikin, District Sidhi for the offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 05.06.2023.

He further submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case and trial will Pushapraj Dwivedi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176483712/
1 take considerable time to be concluded.

sentences.text: He further submits that applicant is a permanent resident of district and is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
According to prosecution, the age of prosecutrix was more than 17 years at the time of incident when she left her parental house.
She stayed with the applicant for about a day.
In her statements recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she has disclosed that on earlier occasion too she spent about three months period with the applicant.
Looking to the age and conduct of the prosecutrix, this Court deems it proper to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Pushapraj Dwivedi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176483712/
